app.title: Interview transcript coder
app.summary: A person opens one participant's interview transcript from a row of tabs and reads it turn by turn. They select a passage within one speaker's turn and click a code in the codebook to apply it, which tints the passage and adds a removable chip beside the turn. Each code shows its definition and how many segments and participants it covers. Codes can be added with a name and definition as the work goes on. A code's Show turns gathers every turn coded with it across all participants, and each one can be opened back in its own transcript. The coded segments are exported as a CSV of participant, turn, speaker, code and text.

task.text: Apply codes from a definable codebook to passages of interview transcripts, see where each code occurs across participants, and export the coded segments.

data.text: A small set of interview transcripts, each an ordered list of interviewer and participant turns, with a codebook of named, coloured, defined codes and the coded segments (character ranges inside a turn, each with one code).
data.item: a passage selected within one speaker's turn of an interview transcript

stage.text: coding interview transcripts with codes added as they emerge, before building themes

mechanism.text: The transcript pane shows one participant's turns with coded passages tinted in their code's colour (overlaps get an underline in a second colour) and code chips per turn. The codebook sidebar beside it applies the code to the pending selection, counts segments per code and per participant, and switches the pane to a cross-participant view of the turns carrying one code, from which a turn can be opened in context.

field.text: inductive qualitative coding of interview transcripts, in the social sciences

workflow.name: apply codes from a codebook to passages of text

steps.here: Participant tabs (P01, P02, P03, each titled with its count of coded segments) switch the transcript pane to that person's interview, headed by a one-line description and the segment count, with interviewer and participant turns numbered.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: Dragging over text inside one turn sets a pending passage (trimmed of spaces, refused if it crosses speakers), shown in the Selected passage box. Clicking a code name applies it, tints the passage and adds a chip with an x to remove it. The same passage cannot get the same code twice, but can get several codes.

steps.step: add to or revise the category set as you go
steps.here: An Add a code form takes a name and a definition (when to apply it and when not to), refuses a duplicate name and gives the new code the next unused palette colour.

steps.step: summarize how often each category is used
steps.here: Each codebook entry shows '<n> segments, <k> of <N> participants' and a per-participant count, faint where zero, or 'Not applied yet'.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Show turns on a code replaces the transcript with every turn coded with it across all participants, with a summary line. Each turn has a jump button that opens it in its own transcript and flashes it.

Export segments (CSV) downloads a dated file of participant, turn, speaker, code name and passage text, ordered by participant, turn and position. Coding is kept in the browser's local storage and can be cleared after a confirm.

distinctive: A passage must sit within a single speaker's turn, so every segment is attributable to the interviewer or one participant.
Each code carries a written definition, including when not to use it, shown at the point of applying it.
Overlapping codes on the same words are drawn as a tint of the first code with an underline in the second.
Code prevalence is counted by participants as well as by segments, so a code's spread across people is visible next to its definition.

parts.title: Participant tabs
parts.summary: A button per participant in the header that opens their transcript and shows how many segments are coded in it.

spans.first: .tabs button[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; }

parts.title: Transcript
parts.summary: One participant's interview as numbered speaker turns, with coded passages tinted by code colour and a chip per code beside each turn, or, when a code is filtered, every turn carrying that code across participants with a jump back into context.

spans.first: .meta { color: var(--muted); margin: 0 0 10px; display: flex; gap: 10px; align-items: center; }

parts.title: Codebook sidebar
parts.summary: The panel beside the transcript holding the selected passage, the codes, the form for new codes and the clear button.

spans.first: main { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 330px; height: calc(100vh - 48px); }

parts.title: Selected passage
parts.summary: Shows the passage waiting to be coded with its participant, turn and speaker, or says what to do next.

spans.first: #selection { border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 10px; background: #fafaf8; font-size: 13px;

parts.title: Codes with counts
parts.summary: Each code with its colour, definition and counts by segment and by participant. Its name applies it to the selected passage, and Show turns filters the transcript to it.

parts.title: Add a code
parts.summary: A name and definition form that adds a new code in the next free colour, refusing duplicate names.

spans.first: #add-code label { display: block; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); margin: 6px 0 2px; }

parts.title: Export and saved state
parts.summary: Keeps codes and segments in the browser's local storage, seeded with a few coded passages, and exports the segments as a dated CSV or clears them after a confirm.

spans.first: function csvCell(v) { const s = String(v); return /[",\n]/.test(s) ? '"' + s.replace(/"/g, '""') + '"' : s; }
